newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude sharpens gains late on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude sharpens gains late on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX crude sharpened gains Friday afternoon on short covering and refiner buying ahead of the May crude contract expiry Tuesday, dealers said.

"The market tried to make new lows all week and couldn't, so we have some frustrated shorts who are covering plus refiners are under pressure to belly up on crude after resisting it all month," said a New York crude trader.
At 1425 EDT, May crude was up 53 cents at $19.95 a barrel, the simple 20-day moving average and technical resistance which was lightly breached at the session high of $19.97.

Crude was also boosted Friday afternoon by news IPL Energy Inc closed four lines on its Interprovioncial pipeline system after reports of a small oil spill. The spill consisted of only 10 barrels, and the company had already restarted one line, and it said the other three would be restarted shortly.
"The IPL news may have played into it psychologically, but it really is not a big deal. Crude was climbing before that," said a New York crude trader.
May gasoline was up 0.85 cent at 61.55 cents a gallon reflecting cash strength in the New York Harbor. May heating oil was up 0.50 cent a gallon at 54.50 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
